attacker_pocs.name: matlab_class_simple_npoints
attacker_pocs.why: Mat_Open + Mat_VarReadNext on a v7.3 MAT-file whose MATLAB_class attribute is a simple dataspace of two fixed-length strings (each length 6, under MAX_CLASS_NAME). Mat_H5ReadVarInfo accepts any H5S_SIMPLE dataspace and H5Aread writes both elements (14 bytes) into a 7-byte buffer. The real fix routes that read through Mat_H5ReadScalarAttribute, which rejects npoints != 1 before the read; this commit never checks the element count.

role_a_rationale: The commit rejects non-string and variable-length MATLAB_class values and caps class_len at MAX_CLASS_NAME, and it reads MATLAB_sparse via Mat_H5ReadScalarAttribute, so ordinary scalar class names and sparse variables still round-trip. It only checks that the class dataspace class is H5S_SCALAR or H5S_SIMPLE and then calls H5Aread, dropping the helper's npoints == 1 test. A two-element fixed string therefore still heap-overflows in Mat_H5ReadVarInfo; the golden tree returns a format error instead.
